headline: Theoretical & Computational Nuclear Physics
subheadline: Nuclear Reaction Dynamics · Superheavy-Element Synthesis · Computational Modelling · Uncertainty Quantification
intro: Research on how superheavy nuclei form in heavy-ion collisions, using stochastic reaction models, model calibration and uncertainty quantification. The same computational methods extend into scientific computing, machine learning and data engineering.
figure_alt: Schematic of superheavy-element synthesis in three stages: capture, compound-nucleus formation and survival. The evaporation-residue cross section is the product of the three.
figure_caption: Superheavy-element synthesis as three stages: capture, formation and survival.
research_text: The central question: which reaction mechanisms govern the formation of superheavy nuclei, and how reliably can they be predicted?

questions.label: How does a touching nuclear system fuse into a compound nucleus, rather than re-separate?
How well can cross sections for new elements such as Z = 119 and 120 be predicted?
Which model parameters do experimental data actually constrain, and with what uncertainty?
